definition_zh: 摇摆；摆动；转身；秋千；转变
definition_en: to move back and forth, or a seat hanging on ropes
core_image: 孩子在秋千上前后荡起，绳子划出弧线
scene: 孩子用力荡着秋千。The child pushed the swing high into the air.
sceneCN: 这里 swing 是「秋千」（第 3 个义项）；句意：孩子把秋千推得很高。

senses.title: To move back and forth
senses.definition: to move backwards and forwards from a fixed point
senses.definitionCN: 从固定点来回移动
senses.example: The lamp swung in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 灯在风中摇摆。
senses.why: The hanging seat gave the word its basic picture of motion around a pivot.
senses.whyCN: 悬挂的座位给这个词提供了绕支点运动的基本画面。

senses.title: To turn sharply
senses.definition: to turn quickly in a particular direction
senses.definitionCN: 朝某方向迅速转动
senses.example: She swung round to face him.
senses.exampleCN: 她转身面对他。
senses.why: A swinging object changes direction, so a person turning quickly is described the same way.
senses.whyCN: 摆动的物体改变方向，于是迅速转身的人也用同样的说法。

senses.title: A seat on ropes
senses.definition: a seat hanging from ropes that a person rides for fun
senses.definitionCN: 用绳索吊起供人玩耍的座位
senses.example: The children queued for the swing.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们排队等秋千。
senses.why: The noun names the very object whose motion produced the verb.
senses.whyCN: 名词指的正是产生这个动词的那种物体。

senses.title: A shift in opinion
senses.definition: a change from one position or opinion to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一种立场或观点转向另一种
senses.example: There was a swing towards the opposition.
senses.exampleCN: 出现了倒向反对派的转变。
senses.why: A pendulum moves to the other side, so a change of opinion is pictured as a swing.
senses.whyCN: 钟摆摆向另一边，于是观点的改变被画成一次摆动。

intro.en: Swing comes from an old Germanic verb for beating or swinging.
intro.cn: swing 源自古老的日耳曼语动词，意为挥打或摆动。

items.en: The root described a sweeping, swinging movement.
items.cn: 该词根描述挥扫、摆动的动作。

items.en: Swingan meant to beat or flog.
items.cn: swingan 意为击打或鞭打。

items.en: Swingen widened to any back and forth motion.
items.cn: swingen 扩展到任何来回运动。

items.en: Swing named the hanging seat children ride.
items.cn: swing 指孩子们玩的悬挂座位。

items.en: Swing extended to shifts of opinion and mood.
items.cn: swing 又扩展到观点与情绪的变化。

note.en: Swing is compared with look-alike words and with words for moving to and fro.
note.cn: 把 swing 与形近词以及表示来回移动的词作比较。

definition_zh: 桌子；表格；一桌人；提交（议案）
definition_en: a piece of furniture with a flat top and legs, or an arranged set of facts
core_image: 木桌中央摆着茶壶，四条桌腿稳稳压住地板
scene: 晚饭已经摆在桌上了。Dinner is already on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 table 是「桌子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：晚饭已经摆在桌上了。

senses.title: A piece of furniture
senses.definition: furniture with a flat top and legs
senses.definitionCN: 有平面与支腿的家具
senses.example: Dinner is already on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭已经摆在桌上了。
senses.why: The Latin word tabula named a flat board, which is exactly the object we still call a table.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tabula 指平板，正是我们今天仍称作桌子的物件。

senses.title: Facts set out in rows
senses.definition: facts arranged in rows and columns
senses.definitionCN: 按行列排列的事实
senses.example: The results are shown in the table below.
senses.exampleCN: 结果见下表。
senses.why: A flat board is where figures were laid out, so an arranged set of facts kept the same name.
senses.whyCN: 平板是摆放数字的地方，因此按规则排列的事实沿用了同一个名字。

senses.title: The people seated together
senses.definition: a group of people sitting at one table
senses.definitionCN: 围坐一桌的一群人
senses.example: The whole table laughed at the story.
senses.exampleCN: 一桌人都被这个故事逗笑了。
senses.why: The furniture stands for the group gathered around it, a common kind of transfer.
senses.whyCN: 家具代指围坐其旁的人群，这是常见的转喻。

senses.title: To present formally
senses.definition: to propose something for discussion
senses.definitionCN: 正式提出供讨论
senses.example: They tabled a motion at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在会上提交了一项动议。
senses.why: A document placed on the table is offered to the assembly, so the noun became a verb.
senses.whyCN: 把文件放到桌上就是提交给会议，于是名词转为动词。

senses.title: To get hold of something
senses.definition: to put your hand on something and hold it
senses.definitionCN: 把手放在某物上并握住它
senses.example: He took the keys from the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他从桌上拿起钥匙。
senses.why: The core act is the hand closing on an object.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作就是手掌合拢抓住一件东西。

senses.title: To carry or bring
senses.definition: to carry something or someone to another place

senses.example: Please take this letter to the office.

senses.why: What is grasped is then carried away.
senses.whyCN: 抓住之后自然就是带走，于是长出「携带」义。

senses.title: To need time

senses.example: The journey takes two hours.

senses.title: To choose or accept

definition_en: a story, especially one that may not be true or is told in an imaginative way
core_image: 炉火边讲述的漫长故事：真假难辨，却让人一直听下去
scene: 祖父在冬夜里讲起年轻时航海遇险的经历，孩子们听得入了迷。The old sailor told a long tale about his voyage across the stormy sea.
sceneCN: 这里 tale 是「故事、叙述」（第 1 个义项：一段讲述出来的故事）；句意是老水手讲述了一段关于自己跨越风暴之海的漫长故事。

derivatives.zh: story（故事）+ teller（讲述者），义为「讲故事的人」
tale + telling（讲述），义为「讲故事；搬弄是非」

senses.title: A story that someone tells
senses.definition: a story that someone tells, often one that is imaginative or entertaining
senses.definitionCN: 某人讲述的一段故事，常带有想象色彩或趣味性
senses.example: Grandmother told us a tale about a clever fox.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母给我们讲了一只聪明狐狸的故事。
senses.why: The core image is someone narrating by the fire: words flow forward and carry listeners into another world.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是有人在炉边开口叙述：话语向前流淌，把听众带进另一个世界，所以最基本义就是「讲出来的故事」。

senses.title: An account of events, real or invented
senses.definition: an account of a series of events, whether true or invented
senses.definitionCN: 对一连串事件的记述，可以是真实的也可以是虚构的
senses.example: The survivor gave a moving tale of the shipwreck.
senses.exampleCN: 幸存者讲述了感人的沉船经历。
senses.why: A narration may carry real experience; the same flowing words can recount actual events, extending the story sense to personal accounts.
senses.whyCN: 叙述既可以承载虚构，也可以承载真实经历：同一股「流淌的话语」被用来记述事件，于是故事义延伸为「经历、记述」。

senses.title: A lie or an unreliable report
senses.definition: a statement or report that is not true or cannot be trusted
senses.definitionCN: 不真实或不可信的说法、传闻
senses.example: Don't believe that tale; it is just gossip.
senses.exampleCN: 别信那种说法，那只是谣言。
senses.why: Because many fireside stories are invented, the word picked up a hint of fabrication, giving the negative sense of untrustworthy talk.
senses.whyCN: 因为炉边故事常是编出来的，这个词沾上了「虚构」的意味，于是引申出「不实之词、谣言」的贬义。

senses.title: A full reveal of past behavior
senses.definition: the whole story that past marks or evidence reveal about someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 痕迹或证据所揭示出的全部情况
senses.example: The worn boots told their own tale of hard travel.
senses.exampleCN: 磨破的靴子诉说着艰苦旅行的经历。
senses.why: Traces speak like a narrator: marks on an object reveal the past just as words tell a story, so evidence itself becomes a tale.
senses.whyCN: 痕迹会像叙述者一样「开口」：物品上的印记揭示过去，正如话语讲述故事，因此证据本身也成了一种「故事」。

senses.title: A traditional legend passed down
senses.titleCN: 传说；口口相传的古老故事
senses.definition: an old story about past people or events that is passed down by word of mouth
senses.definitionCN: 关于过去人物或事件、经口耳相传保留下来的古老故事
senses.example: The village keeps an ancient tale of a hidden treasure.
senses.exampleCN: 村子保留着一个关于宝藏的古老传说。
senses.why: Fireside narration repeats across generations; when the same story travels through many mouths, it hardens into legend.
senses.whyCN: 炉边叙述代代重复：当同一个故事经过无数张嘴流传下来，它就凝固成了「传说」。

senses.title: A long, tedious amount of talk or writing
senses.definition: a long and often boring piece of speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 冗长且常令人生厌的一大段话语或文字
senses.example: He launched into a long tale about his troubles.
senses.exampleCN: 他开始絮絮叨叨地大讲自己的麻烦。
senses.why: The flowing narration can go on and on; when words keep flowing without end, the story becomes tedious length.
senses.whyCN: 叙述可以不断向前流淌：当话语流个不停、没有尽头时，「故事」就变成了「冗长的讲述」。

senses.title: A tale as a literary genre
senses.definition: a work of fiction, especially a short narrative in literary form
senses.definitionCN: 一种叙事性文学作品，尤指短篇故事
senses.example: The book contains six tales of the Middle Ages.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书收录了六个中世纪故事。
senses.why: Spoken stories were later written down and shaped into art; the narration itself became a named literary genre.

intro.en: Tale comes from Old English, sharing a deep root with the verb tell, and its history runs through Germanic storytelling traditions.
intro.cn: tale 源自古英语，与动词 tell 同出一个深层词根，其历史贯穿日耳曼的口述传统。

items.en: The root is generally reconstructed as *talō in Proto-Germanic, connected with counting and speaking, from the idea of counting out words.
items.cn: 该词根一般重构为原始日耳曼语 *talō，与「数、说」相关，来自「数出话语」的观念。

items.en: Old English talu meant tale, speech, and also counting; the same root gave the verb tell, which once meant both to count and to narrate.
items.cn: 古英语 talu 意为故事、言语，也指计数；同一词根派生出动词 tell，后者一度兼指「数数」与「讲述」。

items.en: In Middle English the spelling tale settled, and the counting sense separated into the word tale replaced by number talk and new borrowings.
items.cn: 中古英语时期拼写定型为 tale，「计数」义逐渐分离，讲述义成为主导。

items.en: Chaucer's Canterbury Tales fixed the word as the standard term for a told narrative in English literary tradition.
items.cn: 乔叟的《坎特伯雷故事集》使 tale 成为英语文学传统中「讲述的叙事」的标准用词。

items.en: Today tale suggests an old-fashioned or imaginative story, often with a hint that it may not be fully true.
items.cn: 现代英语中 tale 多指老式或富于想象的故事，常带「未必全真」的意味。

note.en: Tale is easily confused with similar-looking nouns and with near-meaning story words.
note.cn: tale 容易与拼写相近的名词以及近义的故事类词汇混淆。

entries.definitionCN: 以动物为主角、寓意道德教训的寓言

normalIntro.en: Use the root connection and common phrases to remember tale.
normalIntro.cn: 利用词根关联和常见搭配来记忆 tale。

normal.en: Tale shares its root with tell: what you tell becomes a tale.
normal.cn: tale 与 tell 同根：你 tell（讲述）出来的内容就是 tale（故事）。

normal.en: Fairy tale is one of the most common phrases: a fairy tale is an imaginative story.

normal.en: The Canterbury Tales is the classic English work; great tales survive for centuries.
normal.cn: 《坎特伯雷故事集》是英国文学经典：伟大的 tale 能流传数百年。

normal.cn: old wives' tale（无稽之谈）：并非所有 tale 都可信。

abstract.en: Picture a fireside circle where one long tale winds through the winter night.

definition_en: to speak to someone, or a conversation or a speech on a subject
core_image: 两个人在街角站着说话
scene: 两个老朋友在街角站着聊了很久。The two old friends stood at the corner and talked for a long time.
sceneCN: 这里 talk 是「交谈、说话」（第 1 个义项）；句意：两个老朋友在街角站着聊了很久。

senses.title: To speak with someone
senses.definition: to speak to another person in an informal way
senses.definitionCN: 以轻松的方式对另一个人说话
senses.example: The two old friends talked for a long time.
senses.exampleCN: 两个老朋友聊了很久。
senses.why: The verb comes from the same family as tale and tell, the act of putting words between people.
senses.whyCN: 这个词与 tale、tell 同族，核心是人与人之间交换话语。

senses.title: A lecture on a subject
senses.definition: a speech given to an audience about a topic
senses.definitionCN: 就某个题目对听众所作的演讲
senses.example: She gave a talk on climate change.
senses.exampleCN: 她作了一场关于气候变化的讲座。
senses.why: A talk is one voice speaking at length to many.
senses.whyCN: talk 也指一个声音对着许多人长时间讲述。

senses.title: Formal discussions
senses.definition: official discussions between groups or governments
senses.definitionCN: 团体或政府之间的正式商谈
senses.example: The two sides held talks in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在首都举行了会谈。
senses.why: Conversation becomes diplomacy when it is formal and repeated.
senses.whyCN: 谈话一旦正式并且反复进行，就成了外交层面的「会谈」。

definition_zh: 高的；高大的；难以置信的
definition_en: having a greater height than usual, or hard to believe
core_image: 篮球场上最高的少年伸手够到篮筐
scene: 球场上最高的男孩不用跳就够到了篮筐。The tallest boy on the court reached the basket without jumping.
sceneCN: 这里 tall 是「高的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：球场上最高的男孩不用跳就够到了篮筐。

senses.title: Of great height
senses.definition: having a greater height than is usual for a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 高度超过一般人、一般物的
senses.example: The tallest boy on the court reached the basket without jumping.
senses.exampleCN: 球场上最高的男孩不用跳就够到了篮筐。
senses.why: The older sense was brave and fine, and height came to stand for that dignity.
senses.whyCN: 较早的义项是「勇敢、出色」，身材的高大便成了这种气度的象征。

senses.title: Hard to believe
senses.definition: difficult to believe because it is exaggerated
senses.definitionCN: 因为夸张而难以让人相信的
senses.example: He told a tall story about catching a fish as big as a boat.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲了一个荒诞的故事，说他钓到一条船那么大的鱼。
senses.why: A tall tale is a story that stands too high to be true.
senses.whyCN: 「高得离谱的故事」即高到不可能是真的，于是 tall 表示夸张、难信。

definition_zh: 任务；工作；使承担艰巨任务

root: 中世纪拉丁语 tasca（税、义务）经古法语 tasque 进入英语，由「摊派的义务」转为「任务」。

sensesIntro.en: Task began as an imposed duty and settled into a piece of work and the act of assigning it.
sensesIntro.cn: task 从被摊派的义务，固定为一项工作，以及分派工作的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a duty pinned to a desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份被钉在桌上的义务。

branches.en: The work itself is the main sense.
branches.cn: 工作本身是主要义项。

branches.en: Assigning is laying the duty down.
branches.cn: 分派就是把义务放下。

branches.en: Noun and verb mirror each other.
branches.cn: 名词与动词互为一体两面。

branches.en: A task force is a group for one job.
branches.cn: 特别工作组就是为一项任务而设。

branches.en: Blame also assigns a burden.
branches.cn: 责备同样是在派一份负担。

intro.en: Task extends through compounds and inflection.
intro.cn: task 通过复合词与屈折扩展。

latinIntro.en: Task traces to Medieval Latin tasca, a tax or duty.
latinIntro.cn: task 可追溯到中世纪拉丁语 tasca（税、义务）。

items.exampleCN: 分派工作是管理的一部分。

items.meaning: to do several tasks at once

definition_en: the flavour of food, the ability to judge what is good, or to try food with the tongue
core_image: 舌尖刚碰到一勺热汤
scene: 她尝了一口汤，觉得有点咸。She tasted the soup and found it a little salty.
sceneCN: 这里 taste 是「品尝」（第 2 个义项）；句意：她尝了一口汤，觉得有点咸。

senses.title: The flavour of food
senses.definition: the flavour that food or drink has in the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 食物或饮料在口中呈现的滋味
senses.example: The soup has a strong taste of garlic.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤有很浓的蒜味。
senses.why: The core sense is what the tongue reports about food.
senses.whyCN: 核心义项是舌头对食物作出的报告。

senses.title: To try food
senses.definition: to put food or drink in the mouth to find out its flavour
senses.definitionCN: 把食物或饮料放入口中以辨别滋味
senses.example: She tasted the soup and found it a little salty.
senses.exampleCN: 她尝了一口汤，觉得有点咸。
senses.why: The noun became the act of testing flavour.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成了检验滋味的动作。

senses.title: Good judgment of style
senses.definition: the ability to judge what is beautiful or suitable
senses.definitionCN: 判断美与得体的能力
senses.example: Her taste in music is very wide.
senses.exampleCN: 她在音乐上的品味很广。
senses.why: Judging flavour by the tongue became judging quality by the mind.
senses.whyCN: 用舌头判断滋味，扩展为用头脑判断品质。

senses.title: A small experience of something
senses.definition: a short experience that shows what something is like
senses.definitionCN: 让人了解某事滋味的短暂经历
senses.example: He had a taste of success at nineteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他十九岁时初尝成功的滋味。
senses.why: A taste is a small sample, and an experience can be sampled too.
senses.whyCN: 品尝本就是取一小口，人生经历也可以「取一小口」。

intro.en: Taste came from a word meaning to touch and test, not only to eat.
intro.cn: taste 源自「触摸、检验」之词，最初并不只与吃有关。

items.en: Taxare meant to touch sharply and judge.
items.cn: taxare 意为触击并评判。

items.en: Taster meant to touch and try.
items.cn: taster 意为触摸并试验。

items.en: Tasten meant to try food in the mouth.
items.cn: tasten 意为在口中试食物。

items.en: Taste extended to judgment of style.
items.cn: taste 扩展到对风格的判断。

items.en: It also means a small experience.
items.cn: 它还表示短暂的体验。

note.en: Taste is compared with look-alike words and with words for flavour and preference.
note.cn: 把 taste 与形近词以及表示滋味和偏好的词作对比。

entries.definitionCN: 测试；只拼写相近，词源不同

normalIntro.en: Taste began with touching and testing, then settled on the tongue.
normalIntro.cn: taste 从触摸与检验开始，最后落在舌头上。

normal.en: She tasted the soup and found it salty.
normal.cn: 她尝了汤，觉得有点咸。

normal.en: The soup has a strong taste of garlic.
normal.cn: 这汤有很浓的蒜味。

normal.en: Her taste in music is very wide.
normal.cn: 她在音乐上的品味很广。

normal.en: He had a taste of success at nineteen.
normal.cn: 他十九岁时初尝成功。

normal.en: That joke was in poor taste.
normal.cn: 那个玩笑不得体。

abstract.en: Tasting is testing with the tongue.
abstract.cn: 品尝就是用舌头检验。

abstract.en: Style is flavour judged by the mind.
abstract.cn: 品味是头脑评判的风味。

abstract.en: A small taste can teach a whole life.
abstract.cn: 一小口滋味能教会整个人生。

examples.en: She tasted the soup and found it a little salty.
examples.cn: 她尝了一口汤，觉得有点咸。

examples.en: The soup has a strong taste of garlic.
examples.cn: 这汤有很浓的蒜味。

examples.en: Her taste in music is very wide.
examples.cn: 她在音乐上的品味很广。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「忒斯特」——舌尖「忒」地碰到汤，立刻判断出滋味，就是品尝。

root: 拉丁语 taxare（触击、评判）经古法语 taster（触摸、试验）进入英语，由「检验」转为「品尝」。

sensesIntro.en: Taste moves from testing by touch to flavour on the tongue, then to judgment and brief experience.
sensesIntro.cn: taste 从触摸检验，到舌尖滋味，再到判断力与短暂体验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tongue meeting the edge of a spoon.
core.cn: 核心意象：舌尖碰到勺子的边缘。

branches.en: Flavour is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 滋味是日常义项。

branches.en: Tasting is the testing act.
branches.cn: 品尝是检验的动作。

branches.en: Judgment grows from testing.
branches.cn: 鉴赏力从检验中长出。

branches.en: A taste is a small sample of life.
branches.cn: 体验是人生的一小口。

branches.en: Both mean taking a sample.
branches.cn: 两者都表示取一点样本。

intro.en: Taste builds -y, -ful, and -less adjectives.
intro.cn: taste 构成 -y、-ful、-less 三个形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin taxare, to touch and judge, underlies taste through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 taxare（触击评判）经古法语构成 taste 的词源。

definition_en: a hot drink made from dried leaves, the leaves themselves, or an afternoon meal
core_image: 白瓷杯里浮着几片舒展的茶叶
scene: 她给客人倒了一杯热茶。She poured a cup of hot tea for her guest.
sceneCN: 这里 tea 是「茶」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她给客人倒了一杯热茶。

senses.title: A hot drink from leaves
senses.definition: a hot drink made by pouring water over dried leaves
senses.definitionCN: 用热水冲泡干叶制成的热饮
senses.example: She poured a cup of hot tea for her guest.
senses.exampleCN: 她给客人倒了一杯热茶。
senses.why: The drink is the first meaning the word carried into English.
senses.whyCN: 这个词进入英语时，最先指的就是这种饮料。

senses.title: The dried leaves
senses.definition: the dried leaves used to make the drink
senses.definitionCN: 用来冲泡饮料的干叶
senses.example: This tea comes from the hills in the south.
senses.exampleCN: 这种茶叶来自南方的丘陵。
senses.why: The material took the name of the drink it makes.
senses.whyCN: 原料沿用了它泡出的饮料之名。

senses.title: An afternoon meal
senses.definition: a light meal eaten in the late afternoon, often with tea
senses.definitionCN: 傍晚时分进食的便餐，常配茶
senses.example: They invited us to tea on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们请我们周日去喝下午茶。
senses.why: The drink gave its name to the meal served with it.
senses.whyCN: 饮料把名字给了与它一同上桌的那顿饭。

intro.en: Tea travelled from China to Europe through Dutch traders.
intro.cn: tea 经由荷兰商人从中国传到欧洲。

items.en: The word came from a southern Chinese form for tea.
items.cn: 这个词来自中国南方表示茶的读音。

items.en: Dutch thee named the imported leaf.
items.cn: 荷兰语 thee 指进口的茶叶。

items.en: Tea entered English as a luxury drink.
items.cn: tea 作为奢侈饮品进入英语。

items.en: Tea extended to the leaves themselves.
items.cn: tea 扩展到指茶叶本身。

items.en: Tea also named the afternoon meal.
items.cn: tea 又指下午的那顿饭。

note.en: Tea is compared with look-alike words and with other drinks.
note.cn: 把 tea 与形近词以及其他饮料名作对比。

entries.definition: a drink made by steeping herbs

normalIntro.en: Tea is a leaf, a drink, and a meal, all under one short word.
normalIntro.cn: tea 是一片叶子、一杯饮料，也是一顿饭。

normal.en: She poured a cup of hot tea.
normal.cn: 她倒了一杯热茶。

normal.en: This tea comes from the southern hills.
normal.cn: 这种茶叶来自南方丘陵。

normal.en: They invited us to tea on Sunday.
normal.cn: 他们请我们周日喝下午茶。

normal.en: Green tea is popular here.
normal.cn: 绿茶在这里很受欢迎。

normal.en: Let us take a tea break.
normal.cn: 我们休息一下喝杯茶。

abstract.en: A leaf teaches water to become warm and fragrant.
abstract.cn: 一片叶子教水变得温热芬芳。

abstract.en: A drink can name a whole hour of the day.
abstract.cn: 一杯饮料能给一天中的一段时间命名。

abstract.en: One syllable crossed oceans.
abstract.cn: 一个音节越过了大洋。

examples.en: She poured a cup of hot tea for her guest.
examples.cn: 她给客人倒了一杯热茶。

examples.en: This tea comes from the hills in the south.
examples.cn: 这种茶叶来自南方的丘陵。

examples.en: They invited us to tea on Sunday.
examples.cn: 他们请我们周日去喝下午茶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「替」——口渴时这杯热饮「替」你解乏，就是茶。

root: 源自中国南方方言中「茶」的读音，经荷兰语 thee 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Tea names the drink, then the leaf, then the meal that goes with it.
sensesIntro.cn: tea 先指饮料，再指茶叶，再指配茶的那顿饭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white cup with leaves unfolding inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：白瓷杯里叶片慢慢舒展。

branches.en: The drink is the core sense.
branches.cn: 饮料是核心义项。

branches.en: The leaf carries the name too.
branches.cn: 茶叶也使用这个名字。

branches.en: The meal is named after the cup.
branches.cn: 那顿饭因杯子得名。

branches.en: Cup and hour belong together.
branches.cn: 杯与时光连在一起。

branches.en: Drink and leaf are one plant.
branches.cn: 饮料与叶子同出一株。

intro.en: Tea forms compounds such as teapot, teacup, and tearoom.
intro.cn: tea 构成 teapot、teacup、tearoom 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: Tea is a loanword from Chinese, so there is no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: tea 是汉语借词，没有拉丁词根。

definition_en: to help someone learn something by showing or explaining it
core_image: 老师握着孩子的手写下第一个字
scene: 她教村里的孩子读书写字。She teaches the village children to read and write.
sceneCN: 这里 teach 是「教」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她教村里的孩子读书写字。

senses.title: To help someone learn
senses.definition: to show or explain something so that another person learns it
senses.definitionCN: 通过示范或讲解让别人学会某事
senses.example: She teaches the village children to read and write.
senses.exampleCN: 她教村里的孩子读书写字。
senses.why: The oldest sense is to point something out so that it is seen.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是「指出来让人看见」，教学由此发展而来。

senses.title: To give lessons in a subject
senses.definition: to work as a teacher of a subject at a school
senses.definitionCN: 在学校担任某门学科的教学工作
senses.example: He teaches history at the high school.
senses.exampleCN: 他在中学教历史。
senses.why: Pointing out facts became the profession of giving lessons.
senses.whyCN: 把知识指给人看，成了一种职业性的授课。

senses.title: To make someone learn a hard lesson
senses.definition: to show someone the results of their actions in a painful way
senses.definitionCN: 用令人难受的方式让人明白行为的后果
senses.example: The loss taught him to check the figures twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这次损失教他学会核对两遍数字。
senses.why: Experience points out a truth in a way that cannot be ignored.
senses.whyCN: 经验把真相指得让人无法忽视，这就是「教训」。

intro.en: Teach is an Old English verb meaning to show or point out.
intro.cn: teach 是古英语动词，意为显示、指出。

items.en: The root meant to show or point.
items.cn: 词根意为显示、指点。

items.en: Tæcan meant to show and instruct.
items.cn: tæcan 意为显示与教导。

items.en: Techen kept the sense of instruction.
items.cn: techen 保留了教学之义。

items.en: Teach covered both schooling and lessons of experience.
items.cn: teach 兼顾学校教育与经验教训。

items.en: The past form taught became irregular by sound change.
items.cn: 过去式 taught 因音变而成为不规则形式。

note.en: Teach is compared with look-alike forms and with verbs of instruction.
note.cn: 把 teach 与形近形式以及表示教学的动词作对比。

entries.definition: to teach over a long period

normalIntro.en: To teach is to point at the world and say, look here.
normalIntro.cn: teach 就是指着世界说：看这里。

normal.en: She teaches the village children to read.
normal.cn: 她教村里的孩子读书。

normal.en: He teaches history at the high school.
normal.cn: 他在中学教历史。

normal.en: The loss taught him to check twice.
normal.cn: 这次损失教他核对两遍。

normal.en: Can you teach me to swim?
normal.cn: 你能教我游泳吗？

normal.en: She taught herself to play the piano.
normal.cn: 她自学了钢琴。

abstract.en: Teaching is pointing, and learning is seeing.
abstract.cn: 教是手指，学是看见。

abstract.en: A hard loss can be the clearest teacher.
abstract.cn: 惨痛的损失往往是最清楚的老师。

abstract.en: What is shown once can last a lifetime.
abstract.cn: 一次示范能受用一生。

examples.en: She teaches the village children to read and write.
examples.cn: 她教村里的孩子读书写字。

examples.en: He teaches history at the high school.
examples.cn: 他在中学教历史。

examples.en: The loss taught him to check the figures twice.
examples.cn: 这次损失教他学会核对两遍数字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「提取」——老师把知识「提」出来给你，就是教。

root: 古英语 tæcan（显示、指出），源自日耳曼语，核心动作是「指给人看」。

sensesIntro.en: Teach moves from pointing something out to running a class to painful lessons.
sensesIntro.cn: teach 从「指给人看」，到授课，再到令人难受的教训。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand guiding another hand to write.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手握着另一只手写字。

branches.en: Showing is the source sense.
branches.cn: 展示是源义项。

branches.en: Teaching becomes a profession.
branches.cn: 教学成为一门职业。

branches.en: Experience teaches without a classroom.
branches.cn: 经验不需要教室也能教人。

branches.en: Both point knowledge toward a learner.
branches.cn: 两者都把知识指向学习者。

branches.en: Subject and life share one verb.
branches.cn: 学科与人生共用一个动词。

intro.en: Teach gives English teacher and teaching.
intro.cn: teach 衍生出 teacher 与 teaching。

latinIntro.en: Teach is Germanic; Latin docere, to teach, is a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: teach 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 docere（教）是语义对应词。

definition_en: a group of people who play or work together, or to join with someone to do something
core_image: 几匹马被同一副挽具套在一起
scene: 整支球队在雨里坚持训练。The whole team kept training in the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 team 是「队、队伍」（第 1 个义项）；句意：整支球队在雨里坚持训练。

senses.title: A group that plays together
senses.definition: a group of people who play a sport on the same side
senses.definitionCN: 在同一方参加比赛的一个人群
senses.example: The whole team kept training in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 整支球队在雨里坚持训练。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a set of animals yoked to one load.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项是被同一副挽具套住、共同拉东西的一组牲口。

senses.title: A group that works together
senses.definition: a group of people who work together on a task
senses.definitionCN: 为完成一项任务而共同工作的一群人
senses.example: A team of engineers designed the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一组工程师设计这座桥。
senses.why: The yoked animals became any group pulling one goal.
senses.whyCN: 被套在一起的牲口，变成任何朝同一目标用力的群体。

senses.title: To join with someone
senses.definition: to join another person or group to do something together
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人或群体联合做事
senses.example: The two firms teamed up on the project.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司在这个项目上合作。
senses.why: To be in one team is to be yoked to the same task.
senses.whyCN: 在同一个队里，就是被套上同一件差事。

intro.en: Team first meant a set of animals pulling one load.
intro.cn: team 最初指共同拉一副载重的一组牲口。

items.en: The root meant a pulling group.
items.cn: 词根意为共同拖拉的一群。

items.en: Team meant a set of draft animals.
items.cn: team 指一组役畜。

items.en: Team extended to any group with one purpose.
items.cn: team 扩展到任何目标一致的群体。

items.en: Team named sports sides and work groups.
items.cn: team 指运动队与工作组。

items.en: The verb means joining forces.
items.cn: 动词义为合力合作。

note.en: Team is compared with look-alike forms and with words for groups.
note.cn: 把 team 与形近形式以及表示群体的词作对比。

entries.definition: a working group on a ship

normalIntro.en: Team remembers animals in one harness pulling together.
normalIntro.cn: team 记着一副挽具里共同用力的牲口。

normal.en: The whole team kept training in the rain.
normal.cn: 整支球队在雨里坚持训练。

normal.en: A team of engineers designed the bridge.
normal.cn: 一组工程师设计了这座桥。

normal.en: The two firms teamed up on the project.
normal.cn: 两家公司在这个项目上合作。

normal.en: Team spirit carried them through the season.
normal.cn: 团队精神支撑他们走完赛季。

normal.en: Every team member spoke at the meeting.
normal.cn: 每位团队成员都在会上发言。

abstract.en: One harness turns many bodies into one effort.
abstract.cn: 一副挽具把许多身体变成一次用力。

abstract.en: A team is a promise made of shoulders.
abstract.cn: 团队是用肩膀许下的承诺。

abstract.en: Shared load, shared direction.
abstract.cn: 共同的负担，共同的方向。

examples.cn: 整支球队在雨里坚持训练。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「替姆」——彼此「替」着分担，才叫一队人。

root: 古英语 team（一组同轭役畜），源自日耳曼语，由「共同拉载重的一群」引申为「团队」。

sensesIntro.en: Team starts with yoked animals, becomes a sports side, a work group, and the act of joining.
sensesIntro.cn: team 从同轭牲口，变成球队、团队，以及合作的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several horses under one harness.
core.cn: 核心意象：几匹马套在同一副挽具下。

branches.en: The sports side is the daily sense.
branches.cn: 球队是日常义项。

branches.en: Work groups inherit the shared load.
branches.cn: 工作组继承了共同负担。

branches.en: Teaming up is entering one harness.

definition_en: a device for speaking to someone far away, or to call someone using it
core_image: 桌上黑色话筒被拿起来
scene: 他抓起电话，拨通了家里的号码。He picked up the telephone and dialled home.
sceneCN: 这里 telephone 是「电话、电话机」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他抓起电话，拨通了家里的号码。

senses.title: A device for distant speech
senses.definition: a device that carries speech between distant places

senses.example: He picked up the telephone and dialled home.
senses.exampleCN: 他抓起电话，拨通了家里的号码。
senses.why: The Greek parts mean far and voice, which is exactly what the device does.

senses.title: To call someone

note.en: Telephone is compared with look-alike forms and with words for calling.

sensesIntro.en: Telephone names the device first and the act of calling second.

senses.title: The broadcasting system

senses.definitionCN: 把活动画面与声音送到家庭的系统
senses.example: The family sat together watching the match on television.

senses.why: The Greek and Latin parts mean far and sight, and the system carries sight far.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语与拉丁语两部分意为「远」与「视觉」，这套系统正是把视觉送到远处。

senses.title: The industry

definition_zh: 告诉；讲述；吩咐；分辨；告发；显示；数；产生效果
definition_en: to give information by speech or writing, to narrate a story, to order someone to do something, or to be able to distinguish one thing from another
core_image: 一个人凑近另一个人的耳朵，话从口中流出
scene: 夜里孩子缠着母亲讲故事，母亲点了一盏小灯。Grandmother told them a tale of the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 tell 是「讲述」（第 2 个义项：说出故事的内容）；句意：祖母给孩子们讲了一个大海的故事。

pos.zh: 告发；产生效果；（语言）显示

derivatives.zh: 讲述者；银行出纳员（由 tell 加表人后缀构成，指说话或点钞的人）
有说服力的；起作用的（现在分词转形容词，指话语产生效果）
算命者（复合词，tell 保留「预示、说出」义）

senses.title: Give information by speaking
senses.definition: to give information to someone in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 用口头或书面方式把信息告诉某人
senses.example: Tell me your address and I will send the parcel.
senses.exampleCN: 把你的地址告诉我，我把包裹寄出去。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply putting something into words for another person: speech is counted out to a listener.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是把某事用话点给别人听：话语像被「数给」听者。

senses.title: Narrate a story or events
senses.definition: to give an account of a story, or of events in order
senses.definitionCN: 依次讲出故事或事情的经过
senses.example: The grandmother told a tale of the old village.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母讲了一个老村庄的故事。
senses.why: Narration is information stretched into sequence: many small bits of telling are lined up into a whole.
senses.whyCN: 叙述是把信息拉长成序列：许多细小的「告知」连成整体，便成了故事。

senses.title: Order someone to do something
senses.definition: to say to someone that they must do something
senses.definitionCN: 要求或指示某人必须做某事
senses.example: The coach told us to warm up first.
senses.exampleCN: 教练吩咐我们先热身。
senses.why: Speech directed at someone becomes instruction; the telling carries weight, not just information.
senses.whyCN: 话语指向某人时就成了指令；此时的「说」带有分量，不只是传递信息。

senses.title: Distinguish one thing from another
senses.definition: to be able to know or judge the difference between things
senses.definitionCN: 能看出或判断出事物之间的差别
senses.example: I cannot tell the twins apart.
senses.exampleCN: 我分辨不出这对双胞胎。
senses.why: To tell here is to reckon or count out a difference, an old sense of counting that survives in judgment.
senses.whyCN: 此义里的 tell 是「点算」出差别——这是它古老的「数、计」义残留在判断里。

senses.title: Reveal an effect or a state
senses.definition: to show or reveal something, especially strain or age, without words
senses.definitionCN: 无需言语就显露出状况，尤指疲累或年岁
senses.example: The long journey was beginning to tell on his health.
senses.exampleCN: 长途跋涉开始影响他的健康。
senses.why: A state that cannot be hidden is itself telling: facts speak when people stay silent.
senses.whyCN: 藏不住的状态自己在「说话」：人不开口时，事实替他开口，便是 tell。

senses.title: Inform against someone
senses.definition: to report someone secretly to a person in authority
senses.definitionCN: 暗中向掌权者举报某人
senses.example: The boy was afraid his classmate would tell on him.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩怕同学告他的状。
senses.why: Telling takes a dark turn when the listener is authority: the same speech act becomes betrayal.
senses.whyCN: 当听话者变成权威，讲述就转向阴暗面：同一个说话动作成了告发。

senses.title: Count things one by one
senses.definition: to count objects or recite numbers in order, now mainly in fixed phrases
senses.definitionCN: 逐一清点或顺次念数，今多见于固定短语
senses.example: The old phrase tells the beads one by one.
senses.exampleCN: 旧短语里一颗颗数念珠。
senses.why: This is the root sense: tell once meant simply to count, as it still does in teller and all told.
senses.whyCN: 这是词根义：tell 原本就是「数」，至今还活在 teller 与 all told 里。

intro.en: Tell is a native Germanic verb. Its oldest meaning is to count or reckon, from which telling others and telling stories both grew.
intro.cn: tell 是日耳曼本族动词，最古老的含义是「数、点算」，告知与讲故事都由此长出。

items.en: Tellan meant to count, reckon, or enumerate things one by one.
items.cn: 古英语 tellan 意为逐个清点、计算。

items.en: Talu, the related noun, gave both tale and tally, keeping the counting sense.
items.cn: 同源名词 talu 衍生出 tale 与 tally，保留了「数」义。

items.en: The verb goes back to a Germanic root for counting, cognate with German zählen.
items.cn: 动词可追溯至日耳曼语「计数」词根，与德语 zählen 同源。

items.en: The sense moved from counting things to counting out words: informing, narrating and ordering.
items.cn: 词义从「数物」移向「数话」：告知、叙述与吩咐相继出现。

items.en: Judging differences and revealing effects kept the reckoning image, while counting survives only in old phrases.
items.cn: 分辨与显效保留了「点算」意象，而「数」义只留在旧短语中。

note.en: Tell is set beside its Germanic relatives and beside speech verbs that overlap with it.
note.cn: 把 tell 与日耳曼同族词，以及与之交叠的言语动词放在一起对比。

entries.definition: a story, from the same Germanic counting root
entries.definitionCN: 故事；与 tell 同出「计数」词根
计数；记录，保留「点算」古义

entries.definition: a person who tells, or counts money at a bank
to speak words, without the sense of informing a particular person
entries.definitionCN: 说出话来，不含「告知特定对象」的意味

entries.definition: to give a spoken account of events in order
entries.definitionCN: 依次口述事件经过，更书面

entries.definition: to give someone facts, often official

normalIntro.en: Real links: the counting root, the tale family, the bank teller, and the phrase all told.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：计数词根、tale 词族、银行出纳与 all told 短语。

normal.en: Tell once meant to count; all told still means counted altogether.
normal.cn: tell 原义是数；all told 至今意为「总计清点」。

normal.en: Tale and tell are twins: a tale is something told.
normal.cn: tale 与 tell 是孪生兄弟：故事就是被讲述的东西。

normal.en: A bank teller literally counts money for you.
normal.cn: 银行出纳员 teller 字面上就是替你数钱的人。

normal.en: Tell the twins apart: count out the difference between them.
normal.cn: tell the twins apart：把两人之间的差别「点算」出来。

normal.en: Tell on him: your words reach the teacher, and the counting turns into blame.
normal.cn: tell on him：你的话传到老师那里，「点算」变成了指责。

abstract.en: Every sentence is a small counting: word after word handed to a listener.
abstract.cn: 每句话都是一次小小的清点：一个词接一个词递给听者。

abstract.en: Silence also tells: what cannot be hidden speaks by itself.
abstract.cn: 沉默也会说话：藏不住的东西自己开口。

abstract.en: Stories are counted-out time, bead after bead.
abstract.cn: 故事是被一颗颗数出的时光。

examples.en: She told me the truth about the missing key.
examples.cn: 她把钥匙失踪的真相告诉了我。

examples.en: Grandfather told the same story every winter night.
examples.cn: 祖父每年冬夜都讲同一个故事。

examples.en: The strain of the exams is telling on her.
examples.cn: 考试的压力正在影响她。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太欧」——太欧（tel）老师一遍遍数着欧几里得的题，数着数着就讲给你听 → tell 数、讲、告诉

root: 日耳曼本族动词：古英语 tellan「数、点算」，同根名词 talu 给出 tale 与 tally；「告知、讲述」由「逐一数出」引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: From counting things, tell grew into counting out words to a listener, and finally into silent facts that speak.
sensesIntro.cn: tell 从数物出发，长出向听者「数话」的告知与讲述，最终连无声的事实也会 tell。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: counting things out one by one, then counting out words.
core.cn: 核心意象：逐一点数，再逐词「点数」给听者。

branches.en: The root sense survives in old phrases.
branches.cn: 词根义存活于旧短语。

branches.en: Information handed over word by word.
branches.cn: 信息被逐词递交。

branches.en: Many tellings lined up become a story.
branches.cn: 许多次讲述连缀成故事。

branches.en: Speech aimed at a person turns to order or to betrayal.
branches.cn: 指向某人的话语变成命令或告发。

branches.en: Reckoning a difference; facts that speak unbidden.
branches.cn: 点算差别；事实不请自言。

intro.en: Tell belongs to the Germanic counting family shared with tale, tally and talk.
intro.cn: tell 属日耳曼「计数」词族，与 tale、tally、talk 同源相关。

latinIntro.en: Tell is not from Latin; the nearest Latin parallels are reckoning verbs, given here only as contrast.
latinIntro.cn: tell 并非源自拉丁语；此处列出拉丁语中的「计算」动词仅作对照。

items.exampleCN: talu 衍生 tale 与 tally。

items.meaningCN: 数；计算（拉丁来源的对照词）

definition_en: a measure of how hot or cold something is
core_image: 墙上的温度计里，红色液柱停在一个刻度上，室内外差出一大截
scene: 实验室墙上的温度计显示，室内比室外高许多。The thermometer showed a temperature ten degrees higher indoors.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「可测量的冷热程度」（第 1 个义项：温度读数）；句意为温度计显示室内温度比室外高十度。

senses.title: A measured degree of heat
senses.definition: a number expressing how hot or cold a body or space is
senses.definitionCN: 表示物体或空间冷热程度的数值
senses.example: The thermometer showed a temperature ten degrees higher indoors.
senses.exampleCN: 温度计显示室内温度比室外高十度。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'a tempering or moderation'; early science used it for the balance of hot and cold in a body, then for the measured balance itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「调和、适度」；早期科学用它指体内冷热的平衡，后来指被测出的这个平衡。

senses.title: Body heat
senses.definition: the internal heat of a living body, normally around thirty-seven degrees
senses.definitionCN: 活体内部的温度，正常约三十七度
senses.example: The nurse recorded the patient's temperature twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每天记录病人两次体温。
senses.why: A living body regulates its own balance of heat, which is exactly what the old sense of tempering described.
senses.whyCN: 活体自行调节冷热平衡，这正是旧义「调和」所描述的。

senses.title: The weather figure
senses.definition: the outdoor air temperature reported in a forecast
senses.definitionCN: 预报中报告的室外空气温度
senses.example: The forecast gives a temperature of minus five tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 预报说今晚气温为零下五度。
senses.why: Air is a body too, and meteorology applies the same measurement to the atmosphere.
senses.whyCN: 空气也是一种物体，气象学把同一测量用到大气上。

senses.title: A fever
senses.definition: an abnormally high body temperature caused by illness
senses.definitionCN: 疾病引起的异常升高的体温
senses.example: The child has a temperature and should stay home.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子发烧了，应该待在家里。
senses.why: In everyday speech a 'temperature' means the raised figure, not the normal one, so the measurement stands for the illness.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语中 a temperature 指升高的那个数值，而不是正常值，于是测量结果代表了疾病。

senses.title: A device set point
senses.definition: the target temperature set on a thermostat or oven
senses.definitionCN: 在恒温器或烤箱上设定的目标温度
senses.example: Set the temperature to two hundred degrees before baking.
senses.exampleCN: 烘烤前把温度设为两百度。
senses.why: A control dial turns the noun into an instruction: the temperature is what the machine is told to reach.
senses.whyCN: 控制旋钮把这个名词变成指令：温度是机器被要求达到的值。

senses.title: The emotional climate
senses.definition: the general mood or level of tension in a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中的总体情绪或紧张程度
senses.example: The temperature of the debate rose after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 声明发布后，辩论的火气升高了。
senses.why: Social heat is read like physical heat: a room can become hot with anger.
senses.whyCN: 社会的热像物理的热一样被读取：一个房间可以因愤怒而变热。

senses.title: A physical quantity
senses.definition: in physics, a property measuring the average kinetic energy of particles
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中衡量粒子平均动能的属性
senses.example: The temperature of the gas rises as the piston compresses it.
senses.exampleCN: 活塞压缩气体时，气体温度升高。
senses.why: Physics narrows the everyday number to a precise property of a system.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把日常数字收窄为系统的精确属性。

senses.title: A standard condition
senses.definition: the ordinary indoor heat at which materials and reactions are compared
senses.definitionCN: 比较材料与反应时所用的通常室内温度
senses.example: Store the reagent at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 把试剂存放在室温下。
senses.why: Labs need a standard, so 'room temperature' becomes a fixed benchmark rather than a description.
senses.whyCN: 实验室需要一个标准，于是「室温」成了固定基准而不是描述。

intro.en: Temperature comes from Latin temperatura 'a tempering, a due mixture'. The modern physical sense is a later narrowing. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: temperature 出自拉丁语 temperatura「调和、适当的混合」。现代物理义是后来的收窄。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Temperatura meant a mixing in due proportion, from temperare 'to mix, regulate, restrain'.
items.cn: temperatura 意为按适当比例混合，出自 temperare「混合、调节、节制」。

items.en: Temperare is related to tempus 'time, season', because mixing in the right measure was imagined as keeping to the right season.
items.cn: temperare 与 tempus「时间、季节」相关，因为「按正确比例混合」被想象为顺应正确的时令。

items.en: Medieval medicine used temperatura for the balanced mixture of humours in a body, and English borrowed it as temperature in this medical sense.
items.cn: 中世纪医学用 temperatura 指体内体液的有序混合，英语借入时也带这一医学义。

items.en: With the thermometer, the word shifted from a balance of qualities to a measurable degree of heat.
items.cn: 随着温度计的发明，这个词从「性质的平衡」转为「可测量的热度」。

items.en: Physics fixed temperature as a quantity, and everyday speech kept the special phrase 'have a temperature' for fever.
items.cn: 物理学把 temperature 固定为一个物理量，日常口语则保留 have a temperature 这一说法指发烧。

items.en: Room temperature and body temperature became standard benchmarks in labs, kitchens and clinics.
items.cn: 室温与体温成为实验室、厨房与诊所的标准基准。

note.en: Group one separates the temperament words from the temperature word; group two holds related measures and sensations.
note.cn: 第一组分辨 temperament 词族与 temperature 的区别；第二组是相关度量与感觉词。

entries.definition: A person's usual character; it comes from the same Latin root, where a balance of humours was thought to shape personality.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人惯常的性格；出自同一拉丁词根，古人认为体液平衡塑造性格。

entries.definition: To moderate or to become angry easily; the noun means a state of mind, not a degree of heat.
entries.definitionCN: 使缓和，或指容易发怒；名词指心境，而不是热度。

entries.definition: Relating to time or to the material world; it comes from tempus 'time', not from temperare.
entries.definitionCN: 与时间或世俗世界有关；出自 tempus「时间」，而非 temperare。

entries.definition: The energy transferred by a difference in temperature; heat is the cause, temperature is the measured result.
entries.definitionCN: 因温差而传递的能量；热是原因，温度是被测出的结果。

entries.definition: A raised body temperature caused by illness; it names the condition, while a temperature is just the reading.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病引起的体温升高；它指病况，而 temperature 只是读数。

entries.definition: The figure shown by an instrument; a temperature is one kind of reading.
entries.definitionCN: 仪器显示的数字；温度是读数的一种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin family is real, and the measuring instruments are real compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁词族真实存在，测量仪器也都是真实复合词。

normal.en: temperature and temperament share temperare: one measures the body's heat, the other names the body's mix of moods.
normal.cn: temperature 与 temperament 共享 temperare：一个测身体的热，一个指身体性情的混合。

normal.en: thermometer = thermo- (heat) + -meter (measure), the instrument that reads a temperature.
normal.cn: thermometer = thermo-「热」+ -meter「测量」，读取温度的仪器。

normal.en: thermostat = thermo- + -stat (standing, holding), a device that holds a set temperature.
normal.cn: thermostat = thermo- + -stat「保持」，把温度保持在设定值的装置。

normal.en: room temperature is the standard phrase in recipes and lab protocols for ordinary indoor heat.
normal.cn: room temperature 是食谱与实验规程中表示通常室内温度的标准说法。

normal.en: to have a temperature means to be feverish, because the number has gone above normal.
normal.cn: have a temperature 指发烧，因为那个数字高出了正常值。

abstract.en: Abstractly, temperature is balance made countable: hot and cold are weighed against each other and turned into a number.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，temperature 是可数的平衡：冷与热相互权衡，变成一个数字。

abstract.en: The same number can describe a room, a body, a gas or the mood of a meeting.
abstract.cn: 同一个数字可以描述房间、身体、气体，也可以描述一场会议的气氛。

abstract.en: So temperature is not heat itself but heat made comparable.
abstract.cn: 所以 temperature 不是热本身，而是变得可比较的热。

examples.en: The temperature fell below zero before dawn.
examples.cn: 黎明前气温降到了零下。

examples.en: Keep the oven at a constant temperature.
examples.cn: 让烤箱保持恒温。

examples.en: Her temperature returned to normal after two days.
examples.cn: 两天后她的体温恢复正常。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「天不热」：天不热也有温度 → temperature 温度

root: 拉丁语 temperatura「调和、适当混合」← temperare「混合、调节」，与 tempus「时间、季节」相关；十七世纪起经温度计的使用转为可测量的热度。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one measurable balance: a room, a body, the weather, a fever, a thermostat setting, a social mood, a physical quantity and a standard benchmark.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着一个可测的平衡展开：房间、身体、天气、发烧、恒温设定、群体情绪、物理量，以及标准基准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hot and cold weighed against each other and read off as a number.
core.cn: 核心意象：冷与热相互权衡，被读成一个数字。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: everyday heat and the physicist's quantity are the same number at two levels of precision.
branches.cn: 测量：日常热度与物理学家的物理量，是同一数字的两种精度。

branches.en: THE BODY: normal warmth and illness-heat are one scale read above and below the usual line.
branches.cn: 身体：正常体温与病热，是同一条刻度在常线上下两侧的读数。

branches.en: THE AIR: a forecast figure and a lab benchmark both describe ordinary surroundings.
branches.cn: 空气：预报数字与实验室基准都在描述平常环境。

branches.en: CONTROL: a dial turns the noun into a target to be reached.
branches.cn: 控制：旋钮把这个名词变成一个要达到的目标。

branches.en: MOOD: a room heated by anger borrows the same thermometer.
branches.cn: 情绪：被愤怒加热的房间借用了同一支温度计。

intro.en: Temperature belongs to the Latin temperare family. English adds -ature for the noun, while Greek thermo- supplies the instruments.
intro.cn: temperature 属于拉丁 temperare 词族。英语加 -ature 构成名词，希腊语 thermo- 则提供仪器名称。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries below are the recorded ancestors of the family; tempus 'time' is included because temperare was built on the idea of the right season.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁条目是该词族有记录的祖先；列出 tempus「时间」，因为 temperare 建立在「合宜时令」的观念上。

items.meaningCN: 读取温度的仪器（thermo- 表示热，-meter 表示测量）
items.exampleCN: 温度计读数是三十八度。

items.meaning: a device that keeps a set temperature
items.meaningCN: 把温度保持在设定值的装置（-stat 表示保持）
items.example: The thermostat switches the heater off.

items.meaning: to moderate; also a state of mind
items.example: She tempered her criticism with praise.
The temperate zone has four seasons.

items.meaning: kept at a fixed heat by a device
items.example: The samples sit in a temperature-controlled room.

items.meaning: the ordinary indoor heat, used as a benchmark
items.meaningCN: 通常的室内温度，用作基准
items.example: Serve the cheese at room temperature.

items.meaning: the internal heat of a living body
items.example: Body temperature is lowest before dawn.

latinEntries.meaning: to mix in due proportion, regulate

definition_en: a game in which two or four players hit a ball over a net using rackets
core_image: 一张球网隔开两人：球被球拍来回击打过网
scene: 周末清晨，球拍击球的脆响在球场回荡，汗水洒在红色的地面上。We played tennis on the clay court until noon.
sceneCN: 这里 tennis 是「网球运动」（第 1 个义项：一种隔网用球拍击球的球类运动）；句意是我们一直在红土网球场上打球打到中午。

derivatives.zh: table + tennis 复合词，义为「乒乓球」，缩小版网球运动
tennis + elbow 复合词，义为「网球肘」，一种常见于网球运动员的肘部劳损

senses.title: The sport of hitting a ball over a net
senses.definition: a game in which two or four players use rackets to hit a ball back and forth over a net
senses.definitionCN: 由两名或四名运动员用球拍隔着球网来回击球的球类运动
senses.example: She plays tennis every weekend with her sister.
senses.exampleCN: 她每个周末都和姐姐一起打网球。
senses.why: The core image is the net splitting two sides and the ball flying back and forth; the sport itself is named by this single image.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一张网隔开两方、球在空中来回飞：这项运动本身就用这一个画面命名，因此最基本义就是「网球运动」。

senses.title: The ball used in the game
senses.definition: the soft yellow-green ball used in the game of tennis
senses.definitionCN: 打网球所用的黄绿色软球
senses.example: A stray tennis rolled under the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 一个网球滚到了栅栏底下。
senses.why: The name of the game easily transfers to the object the game is played with; the sport lends its name to its ball.
senses.whyCN: 运动的名字很容易转指这项运动所用的器具：运动的名称借给了它使用的球，于是 tennis 也可指「网球（球本身）」。

senses.title: A tennis session or match occasion
senses.definition: an occasion or period of playing tennis
senses.definitionCN: 打网球的一次活动或时段
senses.example: Let's have a quick tennis before lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午餐前我们快点打一场网球吧。
senses.why: Activities are often named without articles in English; the sport name becomes shorthand for one occasion of playing it.
senses.whyCN: 英语里活动名称常可省去冠词直接代指活动本身：运动名成为「打一次」的简称，义为一场网球活动。

senses.title: Tennis as a competitive professional world
senses.definition: the professional world or circuit of tennis competitions
senses.definitionCN: 职业网球赛事构成的世界或圈子
senses.example: She has spent a decade in professional tennis.
senses.exampleCN: 她在职业网坛已打拼了十年。
senses.why: A sport name can stand for the whole community and circuit built around it; playing becomes a career field.
senses.whyCN: 运动名称可代指围绕它建立的全部社群与赛事体系：打球变成一种职业领域，即「网坛」。

senses.title: Tennis as a school or club subject
senses.definition: tennis taught or organized as a course or club activity
senses.definitionCN: 作为课程或社团活动开设的网球项目
senses.example: Tennis is offered as an elective this term.
senses.exampleCN: 本学期开设网球选修课。
senses.why: Institutions name their offerings after the sport; the game becomes a labeled program within school or club life.
senses.whyCN: 学校与俱乐部用运动名来命名所开设的项目：网球运动成为课程表上的一个标签，即「网球课/项目」。

senses.title: Table tennis as a compound
senses.definition: used in compounds such as table tennis for similar net games
senses.definitionCN: 用于 table tennis 等复合词，指类似的隔网球类运动
senses.example: They watched table tennis on television.
senses.exampleCN: 他们看电视转播的乒乓球比赛。
senses.why: The image of hitting a ball over a net is copied at table size; the name travels into smaller versions of the game.
senses.whyCN: 隔网击球的画面被缩小到桌面上：这一运动名迁移到迷你版本，构成「乒乓球」等复合词。

senses.title: A tennis court or facility context
senses.definition: used to label courts, clubs, and equipment for the game
senses.definitionCN: 用于标注网球场、网球俱乐部及器材
senses.example: The tennis club opens at nine.
senses.exampleCN: 网球俱乐部九点开门。
senses.why: Facilities take the sport's name as a label; the game name marks the places where it is played.
senses.whyCN: 场地设施借运动名作标签：运动的名字标记了这项运动进行的场所。

senses.title: Historic real tennis as the original form
senses.titleCN: 历史用法：古式室内网球
senses.definition: real tennis, the older indoor form of the game played in royal courts
senses.definitionCN: real tennis，指起源于宫廷的旧式室内网球
senses.example: Real tennis survives in a few old courts in England.
senses.exampleCN: 古式网球仍在英国少数老球场存续。
senses.why: Before modern lawns, the game was played in walled courts; the historic form keeps the oldest sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 现代草地球场出现之前，这项运动在四壁围合的宫廷球场进行：历史形态保留了该词最古老的义项。

senses.title: Figurative back-and-forth exchange
senses.titleCN: 比喻用法：来回往复的交锋
senses.definition: a situation of actions or words going back and forth like a tennis rally
senses.definitionCN: 比喻言行像网球对打一样来回往复的局面
senses.example: The lawyers kept a tennis of objections and replies.
senses.exampleCN: 律师们你来我往， objections 与答辩不断交锋。
senses.why: The rally image of a ball flying back and forth maps onto any exchange of actions; the game becomes a metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 球来回对打的画面可以映射到任何往复的互动：运动名变成比喻，指你来我往的交锋。

intro.en: Tennis has an unusual etymology: it entered English from Old French as a shout used in the medieval ball game.
intro.cn: tennis 的词源颇为特别：它以中世纪球戏中的喊叫声身份从古法语进入英语。

items.en: The word is generally traced to Old French tenez, meaning hold, receive, the call made when serving the ball.
items.cn: 一般追溯至古法语 tenez（意为「接住、拿着」），是发球时的喊话。

items.en: The name appears in Middle English for the royal court game played indoors with the palm first, then rackets.
items.cn: 中古英语时期该词指宫廷室内球戏，最初徒手击球，后来改用球拍。

items.en: Rackets replaced the bare hand, and the game moved between indoor courts and open play.
items.cn: 球拍取代了徒手击球，游戏在室内球场与露天场地之间流转。

items.en: Modern lawn tennis was codified in the 1870s, giving the word its dominant present meaning.
items.cn: 现代草地网球于十九世纪七十年代定型，赋予了 tennis 如今的主导含义。

items.en: Today tennis means the global racket sport, its ball, and its professional world.
items.cn: 如今 tennis 指全球性的球拍运动、网球本身以及职业网坛。

note.en: Tennis is mostly a unique noun, but compounds and neighboring game words cause confusion.
note.cn: tennis 是较为独特的名词，但复合词与邻近的球类词汇容易造成混淆。

entries.definition: a principle or belief held by a group
entries.definitionCN: 信条、原则。只是拼写相近，词源不同
打网球用的黄绿色球，tennis 的复合名词

entries.definition: the marked court where tennis is played
entries.definitionCN: 网球场，tennis 的复合名词

entries.definition: a racket game played with a shuttlecock over a net
entries.definitionCN: 用羽毛球隔网对打的球拍运动，与网球同类

entries.definition: a team game hitting a ball over a net without rackets
entries.definitionCN: 不用球拍、团队隔网击球的排球运动

entries.definition: a racket game hitting a ball against walls in an enclosed court
entries.definitionCN: 在封闭球场向墙壁击球的壁球运动

normalIntro.en: Use the serve-call origin and common compounds to remember tennis.
normalIntro.cn: 利用发球喊叫的来源和常见复合词来记忆 tennis。

normal.en: Tennis comes from Old French tenez, meaning take it: the server's shout before hitting the ball.
normal.cn: tennis 来自古法语 tenez（接住）：发球者击球前的喊话。

normal.en: Table tennis means table-size tennis: same net image, smaller court.
normal.cn: table tennis（乒乓球）：桌面版的 tennis，同样的隔网画面，更小的场地。

normal.en: A tennis court, a tennis racket, a tennis match: the word labels the whole gear set.
normal.cn: tennis court、tennis racket、tennis match：这个词为整套装备与场合打标签。

normal.en: Wimbledon is the most famous tennis tournament; champions become household names.
normal.cn: 温布尔登是最著名的网球赛事；冠军家喻户晓。

normal.en: Real tennis is the medieval indoor ancestor of modern tennis.
normal.cn: real tennis（古式网球）是现代网球的中世纪室内祖先。

abstract.en: Hear the old server shout tenez before each serve, and the name sticks to the game.
abstract.cn: 想象每次发球前老球员喊一声 tenez，名字便贴在了这项运动上。

abstract.en: Picture a yellow-green ball flying back and forth, drawing an arc over the net.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗黄绿色的球来回飞舞，在球网上空划出弧线。

abstract.en: Feel the rhythm of a rally: hit, reply, hit, like a conversation across the net.
abstract.cn: 感受对打的节奏：击球、回击、再击球，像隔着球网在对话。

examples.en: She won the tennis final in three straight sets.
examples.cn: 她直落三盘赢下网球决赛。

examples.en: The kids hit a tennis against the garage wall all afternoon.
examples.cn: 孩子们整个下午对着车库墙打网球。

examples.en: Their debate turned into a tennis of arguments and counterarguments.
examples.cn: 他们的辩论变成了你来我往的交锋。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「 tennis 」谐音「忒耐死」——打网球忒累，耐力不足可不行。

root: tennis 一般认为源自古法语 tenez（tenir「拿、接」的命令式），是中世纪发球时的喊话「接住！」；词形先指宫廷室内球戏，十九世纪随草地网球定型为现代义。来源说法主流可靠，个别细节（何时由喊叫转成运动名）属一般推断。

sensesIntro.en: Tennis radiates from the sport itself to its ball, a playing occasion, the professional world, compounds, and metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: tennis 从运动本身辐射到网球用球、一次打球活动、职业网坛、复合词用法与比喻用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball flying back and forth over a net between two sides
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗球隔着球网在两方之间来回飞舞

branches.en: The net game itself, from medieval courts to modern lawns
branches.cn: 隔网球戏本身，从中世纪宫廷到现代草地

branches.en: The name lends itself to the ball of the game
branches.cn: 运动名将自身借给它使用的球

branches.en: Play occasions, courses, and facilities take the sport's name
branches.cn: 打球活动、课程与场地设施借用运动之名

branches.en: The whole professional circuit is named by the sport
branches.cn: 整个职业赛事体系以运动名代指

branches.en: The net image copies into compounds and back-and-forth metaphors
branches.cn: 隔网画面复制为复合词与往复交锋的比喻

intro.en: Tennis is a borrowed single word, but it forms many compounds and sport-family terms.
intro.cn: tennis 是借入的单词，但构成了大量复合词与球类运动家族词。

latinIntro.en: Tennis has no Latin relatives; it comes from Old French tenez, from Latin tenere at one further remove.
latinIntro.cn: tennis 没有直接的拉丁同源词；它来自古法语 tenez，间接可追至拉丁语 tenere。

items.example: Tenez! The server called before hitting.
items.exampleCN: 发球者击球前喊道：「接住！」

items.example: tenir la balle, to hold the ball
Latin tenere survives in contain and retain
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 tenere 留存于 contain、retain 之中

items.example: They played table tennis after dinner.
items.exampleCN: 晚饭后他们打了乒乓球。

items.example: The tennis court was freshly lined.
She strung her tennis racket tightly.
items.exampleCN: 她把网球拍的线绷得很紧。

items.example: A tennis ball bounced over the fence.

items.exampleCN: 那位网球运动员每天训练。

items.example: Real tennis is played at Hampton Court.
items.exampleCN: 汉普顿宫仍在进行古式网球。
草地网球始于十九世纪七十年代。

derivatives.zh: table + tennis 复合词，义为「乒乓球」

definition_zh: 学期；术语；条款；期限；措辞；把…称为
definition_en: a fixed period of time, a word with a special meaning, a condition of an agreement, or a school period
core_image: 一块立在时间线上的界石，也立在词典与合同里
scene: 新学期第一课，老师在黑板上写下这门课最难的术语。Students must learn the technical terms of biology.
sceneCN: 这里 term 是「术语」（第 2 个义项：专门领域的固定用语）；句意：学生必须学习生物学的专业术语。

collocations.phrase: under the terms of the contract

derivatives.zh: 末端的；终点站（同根形容词与名词）
术语体系（term 加 -logy 构成）

senses.title: A fixed period of time
senses.definition: a set length of time, especially a school term or an office term
senses.definitionCN: 固定的时段，尤指学期或任期
senses.example: The autumn term begins in September.
senses.exampleCN: 秋季学期九月开始。
senses.why: The root is a boundary stone: a term is the space between two marks in time.
senses.whyCN: 词根是界石：term 就是时间线上两个界标之间的一段。

senses.title: A word with a special meaning
senses.definition: a word or expression with a precise meaning in a field
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域具有精确含义的词或表达
senses.example: Photosynthesis is a basic term in botany.
senses.exampleCN: 光合作用是植物学的基本术语。
senses.why: A boundary in language: the word marks exactly where one meaning stops and another begins.
senses.whyCN: 语言中的界石：这个词精确标出意义与意义之间的边界。

senses.title: A condition of an agreement
senses.definition: one of the conditions of a contract or agreement, usually plural
senses.definitionCN: 合同或协议的条件之一，多用复数
senses.example: They agreed to the terms of the lease.
senses.exampleCN: 他们同意了租约条款。
senses.why: Terms are the boundary lines drawn inside an agreement: each clause ends a dispute before it starts.
senses.whyCN: 条款是协议内部的界线：每一条都在争执发生前划下终点。

senses.title: A way of expressing something
senses.definition: the particular words or style used to express something, in terms of or in plain terms
senses.definitionCN: 表达某事所用的话语或风格，用于 in terms of 等
senses.example: Explain the plan in simple terms.
senses.exampleCN: 用简单的措辞解释这个计划。
senses.why: Choosing terms is placing markers in speech: the same thing can be fenced with different words.
senses.whyCN: 选词就是在言语里立界标：同一件事可以用不同的词围出不同的说法。

senses.title: To give a name to
senses.definition: to describe or name something in a particular way, usually passive
senses.definitionCN: 以特定方式称呼或描述，多用被动
senses.example: The project was termed a great success.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目被称为巨大成功。
senses.why: To term is to attach a fixed label, fixing the boundary of what a thing shall be called.
senses.whyCN: to term 就是贴上固定标签，划定某物名称的边界。

senses.title: The end of a pregnancy or of life
senses.definition: the end of a pregnancy carried full time, or the end of life, in full term or in terminally ill contexts
senses.definitionCN: 妊娠足月，或生命的末期，见于 full term 等
senses.example: The baby was born at full term.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿足月出生。
senses.why: The boundary sense returns literally: the end mark of gestation or of life.
senses.whyCN: 「界石」义字面回归：妊娠或生命终点的标记。

intro.en: Term comes from Latin terminus, the boundary stone, the same root as terminal and terminate.
intro.cn: term 源自拉丁语 terminus「界石」，与 terminal、terminate 同根。

items.en: Terminus named a boundary stone and its guardian god.
items.cn: terminus 既指界石，也是守护边界之神的名字。

items.en: The deeper origin of terminus is debated; links to words for stake or fixed mark are proposed but unproven.
items.cn: terminus 的更早来源有争议；与「木桩、固定标记」的联系有此一说但未确证。

items.en: Old French terme passed the word to English in two shapes of meaning: time-limit and expression.
items.cn: 古法语 terme 把「时限」与「用语」两义传给英语。

items.en: Medieval schools fixed the school-term sense and logic used term for a concept word.
items.cn: 中世纪学校确立了学期义，逻辑学用 term 指概念词。

items.en: Contracts, science and computing multiplied the word: terms of service, term paper.
items.cn: 契约、科学与计算使该词激增：服务条款、学期论文。

note.en: Term is compared with its boundary-word family and with words for periods and expressions.
note.cn: 把 term 与「界石」词族及表示时段、用语的词对比。

entries.definition: at the end; an end station
the past form of the verb term
entries.definitionCN: 动词 term 的过去式

entries.definition: a word or phrase used to say something
the last time by which something must be done

normalIntro.en: Real links: terminus the stone, the school calendar, contract clauses, and in terms of.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：界石 terminus、校历、合同条款、in terms of。

normal.en: Terminus marks where the field stops; term marks where time or meaning stops.
normal.cn: terminus 标记田地止步处；term 标记时间或意义的止步处。

normal.en: The autumn term is a fenced stretch of the year.
normal.cn: 秋季学期是被围起来的一段年历。

normal.en: Technical terms are words with fences around them.
normal.cn: 术语就是围了栅栏的词。

normal.en: Come to terms with it: draw the boundary and accept it.
normal.cn: come to terms with：划下界线并接受。

normal.en: In the long term: beyond the next boundary stone.
normal.cn: in the long term：越过下一块界石之后。

abstract.en: A term is a fence you agree to stand inside.
abstract.cn: term 是你同意站进去的一道栅栏。

abstract.en: Every definition begins by placing a stone.
abstract.cn: 每个定义都从立一块石头开始。

abstract.en: To name a thing is to end its vagueness.
abstract.cn: 为事物命名，就是终结它的模糊。

examples.en: The new term starts on the first Monday of September.
examples.cn: 新学期于九月第一个周一开学。

examples.en: Photosynthesis is a term every biology student learns.
examples.cn: 光合作用是每个生物学生都要学的术语。

examples.en: Read the terms before you sign the contract.
examples.cn: 签约前先读一遍条款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特姆」——特别准的时刻表，一学期一换 → term 学期、术语

root: 拉丁语 terminus「界石、端点」→ 古法语 terme → 英语 term；本义为边界，引申为时间边界（学期、期限）、语言边界（术语、措辞）。

sensesIntro.en: One stone, many fences: the calendar term, the contract term, the technical term.
sensesIntro.cn: 一块石头，多种栅栏：校历的学期、合同的条款、专业的术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary stone planted in time and in language.
core.cn: 核心意象：插在时间与语言里的界石。

branches.en: The calendar is a row of stones.
branches.cn: 日历是一排界石。

branches.en: A term fences one meaning inside a field.
branches.cn: 术语把一个意义围在领域之内。

branches.en: Clauses are fences agreed by two hands.
branches.cn: 条款是两只手共同竖起的栅栏。

branches.en: To speak is to place stones in the air.
branches.cn: 说话就是在空中立石。

branches.en: The body also keeps its own calendar.
branches.cn: 身体也保有自己的历法。

intro.en: Term shares the terminus family with terminal, terminate and terminology.
intro.cn: term 与 terminal、terminate、terminology 同属 terminus 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin terminus, boundary stone, is the base; its deeper origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 词基为拉丁语 terminus「界石」；其更早来源不确定。

items.meaning: a period; a word; a condition

definition_zh: 可怕的；骇人的；糟糕的；严重的
definition_en: causing fear or shock; or extremely bad in quality
core_image: 夜里关灯后墙上的影子突然张大嘴
scene: 山路拐弯处，司机看见对面车灯猛地扑来。The crash was a terrible sight.
sceneCN: 这里 terrible 是「骇人的」（第 1 个义项：令人恐惧的）；句意：车祸现场骇人。

derivatives.zh: 非常；可怕地（形容词加 -ly 构成）

senses.title: Causing fear or horror
senses.definition: making people very frightened
senses.definitionCN: 使人极度恐惧的
senses.example: The storm made a terrible noise on the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨在屋顶上发出骇人的声响。
senses.why: The root terrere means to frighten: this is the fright itself in adjective form.
senses.whyCN: 词根 terrere 意为吓人：此义就是恐惧本身的形容词形态。

senses.title: Very bad in quality
senses.definition: of very poor quality or standard
senses.definitionCN: 质量或水准极差的
senses.example: The food at that hotel is terrible.
senses.exampleCN: 那家旅馆的饭菜糟透了。
senses.why: Shock at badness borrows the fright word: what is awful is treated as what scares.
senses.whyCN: 对「差」的震惊借用了恐惧词：糟到令人「害怕」的程度。

senses.title: Very great in degree
senses.definition: extreme in amount or force
senses.definitionCN: 程度或力度极大的
senses.example: The wall felt a terrible pressure in the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水对墙体形成巨大压力。
senses.why: Fear once measured size: the terrible force is one that dwarfs the person facing it.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧曾被用来度量大小：可怕之力就是令人自感渺小之力。

senses.title: Feeling unwell or upset
senses.definition: feeling very ill or unhappy, as in feel terrible
senses.definitionCN: 感到极不舒服或难过，用于 feel terrible
senses.example: She felt terrible after the argument.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵之后她难受极了。
senses.why: The inner state is described with the outer shock word: the body is under attack by feeling.
senses.whyCN: 用外在的震惊词形容内在状态：身体仿佛被情绪袭击。

intro.en: Terrible comes from Latin terribilis, to be feared, built on terrere, to frighten.
intro.cn: terrible 源自拉丁语 terribilis「令人畏惧的」，词基为 terrere「使恐惧」。

items.en: Terrere meant to frighten away or alarm.
items.cn: terrere 意为吓退、惊骇。

items.en: Terribilis described a thing that deserves fear.
items.cn: terribilis 形容值得畏惧之物。

items.en: Old French terrible fixed the spelling and the strong sense.
items.cn: 古法语 terrible 固定了拼写与强义。

items.en: English used terrible of God, war and punishment before everyday badness.
items.cn: 英语先用 terrible 形容神、战争与刑罚，后才用于日常的「差」。

items.en: Everyday use weakened the fear to simple badness or intensity.
items.cn: 日常用法把恐惧弱化为单纯的「差」或程度。

note.en: Terrible is compared with its fear family and with words for very bad things.
note.cn: 把 terrible 与恐惧词族及表示极差的词对比。

entries.definition: the adverb meaning very or frighteningly

entries.definitionCN: 原为吓人的，今为极好的

entries.definition: extremely bad, with dread in the root
entries.definitionCN: 糟糕透顶的（词根含恐惧）

normalIntro.en: Real links: terrere to frighten, the terror family, and the everyday terrible weather.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：terrere「吓人」、terror 词族、日常的 terrible weather。

normal.en: Terrere means to frighten: terrible things make you gasp.
normal.cn: terrere 意为吓人：terrible 之事令人倒吸冷气。

normal.en: Terrific flipped its fear into praise.
normal.cn: terrific 把恐惧翻转成了称赞。

normal.en: Terrible weather is bad enough to scare a picnic.
normal.cn: terrible weather 糟到能吓跑野餐。

normal.en: Feel terrible: the shock turned inward.
normal.cn: feel terrible：震惊转向了体内。

normal.en: Terror is the noun, terrible the adjective, terribly the degree.
normal.cn: terror 是名词，terrible 是形容词，terribly 是程度。

abstract.en: Badness is measured in gasps.
abstract.cn: 「差」是用倒吸的冷气来计量的。

abstract.en: Some words age from terror into complaint.
abstract.cn: 有些词从恐怖老成了抱怨。

abstract.en: Fear once drew the map of size and strength.
abstract.cn: 恐惧曾描画大小与强弱的地图。

examples.en: The earthquake was terrible in both size and loss.
examples.cn: 这次地震无论规模还是损失都极为可怕。

examples.en: He made a terrible first impression at the interview.
examples.cn: 他在面试上留下了糟糕的第一印象。

examples.en: She felt terrible about forgetting the meeting.
examples.cn: 她为忘了会议而难受。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太惹怖」——太惹人怖了 → terrible 可怕的、糟糕的

root: 拉丁语 terrere「使恐惧」→ terribilis「令人畏惧的」→ 古法语 terrible → 英语 terrible；terrify、terror 同根。

sensesIntro.en: From holy fear to everyday complaint: one adjective covers shock, badness and degree.
sensesIntro.cn: 从对神的敬畏到日常抱怨：一个形容词覆盖震惊、差劲与程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gasp at something too big or too bad.
core.cn: 核心意象：面对过大或过糟之物的一声惊呼。

branches.en: The fright itself.
branches.cn: 恐惧本身。

branches.en: Badness big enough to scare.
branches.cn: 大到吓人的差劲。

branches.en: Size expressed through fear.
branches.cn: 用恐惧表达的规模。

branches.en: The gasp turned inward.
branches.cn: 惊呼转向内心。

branches.en: The scale slides from horror to complaint.
branches.cn: 尺度从惊骇滑向抱怨。

intro.en: Terrible belongs to the terrere fear family shared with terrify and terror.
intro.cn: terrible 属 terrere「恐惧」词族，与 terrify、terror 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin terrere, to frighten, gave terribilis, terror and the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 terrere「使恐惧」产生 terribilis、terror 及英语词族。

definition_zh: 测试；检验；试验；化验；考查；测验
definition_en: to try something to see whether it works or is true, or an examination and similar trial used to measure quality or knowledge
core_image: 把东西放进火里、放进仪器里，看它到底行不行
scene: 实验台上摆着新电池和一盏小灯。The engineer used the lamp to test the battery.
sceneCN: 这里 test 是「检验、测试」（第 1 个义项：试验某物以看其性能）；句意：工程师用小灯来测这块电池。

derivatives.zh: 测试员；测试器（test 加表人或表物后缀构成）
测试；检测（动名词，指测试这件事）
易怒的（与 test 无词源关系，仅形近；源自法语 teste「头」）
证明；圣约（源自拉丁 testari「作证」，与 test 同出「见证」意象）

senses.title: Try something to see if it works
senses.definition: to try or examine something in order to discover whether it works or has the wanted quality
senses.definitionCN: 试用或检查某物，以发现其是否有效或具备想要的品质
senses.example: Engineers test every bridge model before building it.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在建桥之前会测试每一个桥梁模型。
senses.why: The core image is the trial: something is put under stress so that its hidden quality shows itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是「试炼」：把东西置于压力之下，让隐藏的品质显形。

senses.title: Check a person's knowledge or skill
senses.definition: to give someone questions or tasks in order to measure their knowledge or ability
senses.definitionCN: 给某人出题或任务以衡量其知识或能力
senses.example: The final test covers all five units of the book.
senses.exampleCN: 期末测验涵盖本书全部五个单元。
senses.why: A trial applied to a person becomes an exam: stress is questions instead of weights.
senses.whyCN: 施加于人的「试炼」就成了考试：压力从重物换成了题目。

senses.title: Medically examine a sample
senses.definition: to examine a sample of blood, urine or other material for signs of illness or substances
senses.definitionCN: 检查血液、尿液等样本以发现疾病或物质
senses.example: Nurses will test the blood sample this afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 护士今天下午会化验这份血样。
senses.why: Examination under controlled conditions is still a trial, only run in a laboratory.
senses.whyCN: 在受控条件下检查仍是「试炼」，只是搬进了实验室。

senses.title: An examination as an event
senses.definition: a written or spoken examination of knowledge or ability
senses.definitionCN: 对知识或能力的笔试或口试
senses.example: She stayed up all night before the driving test.
senses.exampleCN: 驾照考试前她熬了通宵。
senses.why: The act of testing becomes the name of the event in which the act happens.
senses.whyCN: 测试行为转而命名其发生的那场事件。

senses.title: A trial that reveals true quality
senses.definition: a difficult situation that shows what someone or something is really like
senses.definitionCN: 显示出人或物真实品质的困难处境
senses.example: The long delay put everyone's patience to the test.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的延误考验了每个人的耐心。
senses.why: Difficulty works like the laboratory stress: it separates real quality from claimed quality.
senses.whyCN: 困难起到实验室压力的作用：把真实品质与宣称的品质分开。

intro.en: Test comes from Latin testum, an earthen pot used by alchemists to heat metals. Trying metal in the pot became trying anything, and the word drifted through Old French into English.
intro.cn: test 源自拉丁语 testum——炼金术士焙烧金属用的陶罐。在罐中试炼金属演变为试炼一切，这个词经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Testum meant an earthen vessel, especially the cupel in which gold and silver were refined by fire.
items.cn: testum 意为陶器，尤指用火提炼金银的灰皿。

items.en: Assaying metal in the pot gave the metaphor: purity is what survives the fire.
items.cn: 在罐中检验金属形成了隐喻：纯度就是经火之后剩下的东西。

items.en: Old French test kept both the vessel and the trial of metal, and added the sense of proving a claim.
items.cn: 古法语 test 同时保留器皿与试金之义，并加上「证明主张」的义项。

items.en: English took test in the 14th century as a vessel for refining metal, used by alchemists.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 test，指炼金术士提炼金属的容器。

items.en: By the 16th to 17th century the metaphor had won: tests of loyalty, of courage, and finally school tests.
items.cn: 至十六七世纪，隐喻占了上风：忠诚的考验、勇气的考验，最终是学校的考试。

note.en: The first group shows words that only look like test; the second ranks the words English uses for measuring trials.
note.cn: 第一组是形近词；第二组排列英语中各种「测验类」词。

entries.definition: irritable and quick-tempered; the spelling is a coincidence, from a French word for head
entries.definitionCN: 易怒的；拼写巧合，源自法语「头」一词，与 test 无关

entries.definition: proof or evidence; from Latin testari to witness, sharing the idea of proving, not the pot
entries.definitionCN: 证明；圣约；源自拉丁 testari「作证」，共享「证明」意象而非陶罐

entries.definition: to give evidence in court; from the same Latin proving family as testament
entries.definitionCN: 作证；与 testament 同出拉丁「见证」词族

entries.definition: a formal test, often longer and more official; exam is the short form
entries.definitionCN: 正式考试；常更长更正式，exam 为缩略

entries.definition: a short informal test, often for fun or quick checking
entries.definitionCN: 简短随意的测验，常用于娱乐或快查

entries.definition: a test in real conditions, often of endurance rather than knowledge
entries.definitionCN: 现实条件下的试用，常考验耐力而非知识

normalIntro.en: Real links: the alchemist's pot, the gold that survives fire, the blood test, and the driving test.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：炼金术士的陶罐、经火犹存的真金、血液化验、驾照考试。

normal.en: Test began as a pot in which metal was tried by fire.
normal.cn: test 最初是火中试金的容器。

normal.en: Only pure gold survives the fire, so test means finding what is real.
normal.cn: 只有真金经得住火，所以 test 就是找出真货。

normal.en: A blood test is the old pot in modern glass tubes.
normal.cn: 血液化验就是装进现代玻璃管的旧陶罐。

normal.en: Test the water first: dip a toe before diving in.
normal.cn: test the water：下水前先用脚尖试水。

normal.en: Put your patience to the test: the fire now burns your temper.
normal.cn: 「put one's patience to the test」：这一回火烧的是你的脾气。

abstract.en: Every test is a small fire that burns away the claims and leaves the facts.
abstract.cn: 每场测试都是一小簇火，烧掉宣称，留下事实。

abstract.en: Pressure does not create quality; it reveals it.
abstract.cn: 压力不创造品质，它只是显影品质。

abstract.en: A question is a weight placed on the mind to see if it holds.
abstract.cn: 问题就是压在头脑上的重物，看它撑不撑得住。

examples.en: The lab will test the water samples for lead.
examples.cn: 实验室将检测水样中的铅。

examples.en: He passed his driving test on the first attempt.
examples.cn: 他一次就通过了驾照考试。

examples.en: Months of delays tested the team's patience.
examples.cn: 数月的拖延考验着团队的耐心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贴死它」——考试时把答案死死贴在桌上也考不过，还得老老实实测 → test 测试、考验

root: 拉丁语 testum「陶罐、试金灰皿」→ 古法语 test → 英语；由「火中试金」引申出一切测试、考试与考验。

sensesIntro.en: From the alchemist's pot, test grew into trying things, examining people, checking samples, naming the exam itself, and finally any hardship that reveals true quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 从炼金陶罐出发，test 长出试物、考人、验样本、命名考试，最终指一切显露真实品质的艰难处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: metal tried in fire, purity revealed by what survives.
core.cn: 核心意象：火中试金，靠剩下来的东西显出纯度。

branches.en: Trying an object under stress is the oldest branch.
branches.cn: 对物件施压试验是最老的一支。

branches.en: The same trial pointed at a person becomes an exam.
branches.cn: 同一试炼指向人便成了考试。

branches.en: Laboratory checks and exam events carry the pot into modern life.
branches.cn: 化验与考试把陶罐带进现代生活。

branches.en: Hardship is the fire; character is the gold.
branches.cn: 困难是火，品格是真金。

branches.en: What survives the trial is the only honest answer.
branches.cn: 经试炼而存者，才是唯一诚实的答案。

intro.en: Test is short and mostly stands alone; the family adds -er, -ing, and the separate Latin witness family of testify and testament.
intro.cn: test 本身短小、多独立使用；词族加上 -er、-ing，另有源自拉丁「见证」的 testify 与 testament 一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin testum is the pot; a different Latin root, testis meaning witness, gives testify, testament and attestation. The two families share spelling, not origin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 testum 是陶罐；另一个拉丁词根 testis「见证人」给出 testify、testament 与 attestation。两族拼写相近，来源不同。

items.meaning: a person or device that tests
items.example: A breath tester checks the driver.

items.meaning: the act or process of testing
items.example: Testing of the vaccine took two years.

items.meaning: to give evidence as a witness
items.example: She testified in court for three hours.
His testimony freed the innocent man.
items.exampleCN: 他的证词洗清了无辜者的罪名。

items.meaning: proof; also a will; the Bible's two covenants
items.example: The ruins are a testament to the old city's wealth.
items.exampleCN: 遗迹是古城富庶的证明。

items.meaning: to confirm that something is true
items.exampleCN: 专家证实了这幅画的年代。

items.meaning: a glass tube for laboratory tests
items.example: The baby was conceived in a test tube.
items.exampleCN: 这个婴儿是试管受孕的。

items.meaning: a case tried to set a legal precedent
items.example: The court chose it as a test case.
